newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary union members may face farm problems.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary union members may face farm problems.

text.p: European Union member states which adopt a single European currency in 1999 may experience problems when they end the so-called green rate system, European Commission agrimonetary manager Jean Marc Gazagnes, said.
"Transition difficulties can be foreseen when the 'In' member states abolish the agrimonetary system," Gazagnes told an Agra Europe conference.

Gazagnes said that market prices and especially direct aids to producers may face considerable difficulties or they may be relatively minor depending on the monetary or market situations at the end of 1998.

Some member states will not join the monetary union, keeping national currencies for a long time, he added, noting the prospective membership of new countries from eastern Europe and time needed for their adapting to EU rules.
"An agrimonetary system will be needed for the 'Outs' and for trade between 'Ins' and 'Outs,'" he added.
Farmers and the food industry in the 'In' countries will benefit from greater currency and income stability, he said.
Germany, France, Belgium, Netherlands and Luxembourg, accounting for nearly 50 percent of EU agricultural production and 60 percent of intra-EU farm trade, are expected to join the monetary union.
